claims.text: Annael was the leader of a small group of Grey-elves at Mithrim, having the swan as his token.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), Unfinished Tales, "Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin", pp. 17-25

claims.text: While Rían was hosted by the Grey-elves at Lake Mithrim during the birth of her son Tuor, she asked them to foster him, as she wished to part in search of her husband Huor. Annael explained to her how Huor had died, and she left to die at the Hill of the Slain. Thus Annael became the foster-father of Tuor during his early years.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), Unfinished Tales, "Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin", pp. 17-25; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of Túrin Turambar"; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of Tuor and the Fall of Gondolin"

claims.text: As years passed, in order to seek refuge from Easterlings and Orcs, Annael led his small group of people to the caves of Androth. When Tuor was sixteen years of age, Annael had to prevent him from going to fight against the enemies of his House, foreseeing that Morgoth's power would not be defeated until Thangorodrim was overthrown, and that they had to march South to Annon-in-Gelydh, which was built by Turgon long ago. Tuor was much intrigued by the name of Turgon and wished to meet him, but Annael told him how well hidden Turgon's realm was.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), Unfinished Tales, "Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin", pp. 17-25

claims.text: Despite having parted in secret from Androth, Annael's people were located and ambushed by a large force of Orcs and Easterlings. The Elves were all scattered, and Tuor was captured. However, Annael and many of his folk escaped Dor-lómin and joined Círdan in the distant south of Beleriand.
claims.cite: J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), Unfinished Tales, "Of Tuor and his Coming to Gondolin", pp. 17-25; J.R.R. Tolkien, Christopher Tolkien (ed.), The Silmarillion, "Quenta Silmarillion: Of Tuor and the Fall of Gondolin"
